evidence.quote: Abstract. This study investigates the relationship between adolescent physical attractiveness and drug-taking behaviour, emphasizing the human capital and “pretty girl” efects on the decision to use drugs. Through the

human capital efect, physically attractive adolescents are better positioned to accumulate human capital at a young age compared to their less attractive peers. Building on the economics and psychology literature, we

propose a “pretty girl” efect by suggesting that physically attractive young women or girls are more likely to be approached by men or mature boys who may have access to drugs, and they are thus more likely to take

evidence.quote: We test our hypothesis using a public-use sample from the first and fourth waves of the National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent Health (Add Health) in the United States. This longitudinal study is considered a

representative sample of adolescents. Add Health conducted wave 1 from 1994 to 1995, during which the respondents were initially in grades 7 to 12, and then followed the respondents into adulthood. In wave 4 (2008), the
respondents’ ages ranged from 24 to 33. This dataset contains information on the family, school, physical attractiveness and participation in risky behaviour of the respondents.
